parts.text: The equation shows the reaction of calcium carbonate with dilute hydrochloric acid. CaCO 3 (s) + 2HC l (aq) CaC l 2 (aq) + CO 2 (g) + H 2 O(l)

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Small pieces of calcium carbonate react with excess dilute hydrochloric acid of different concentrations. The time taken for each reaction to finish is recorded. The concentrations of dilute hydrochloric acid used are: • 0.75 mol / dm 3 • 1.50 mol / dm 3 • 3.00 mol / dm 3 . All other conditions stay the same. Table 4.1 shows the time taken for each reaction to finish. Table 4.1 concentration of dilute hydrochloric acid in mol / dm 3 time taken for reaction to finish in s 16 32 8

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Copper( II ) chloride crystals are prepared by reacting dilute hydrochloric acid with excess solid copper( II ) oxide. Name the method used to remove any unreacted solid copper( II ) oxide from the reaction mixture. .............................................................................................................................................
